title: Kubernetes by Example
description: Everything you need to run something real, taught in order, against one project small enough to fit on a laptop and complete enough to break properly.
excerpt: Everything you need to run something real, taught in order, against one project small enough to fit on a laptop and complete enough to break properly.

title: Kubernetes by Example 01: The Object Model
description: Why kubectl apply saying “created” tells you almost nothing — and what is really going on in the ten seconds afterwards.
excerpt: Why kubectl apply saying “created” tells you almost nothing — and what is really going on in the ten seconds afterwards.

title: Kubernetes by Example 02: Pods and Containers
description: It ran perfectly in Docker. You put it in a Pod and it died. Here is what a Pod actually is, and why that difference matters more than it looks.
excerpt: It ran perfectly in Docker. You put it in a Pod and it died. Here is what a Pod actually is, and why that difference matters more than it looks.

title: Kubernetes by Example 03: Labels and Selectors
description: Nothing in Kubernetes finds anything by name. Once you know what it does instead, half the surprising behaviour stops being surprising.
excerpt: Nothing in Kubernetes finds anything by name. Once you know what it does instead, half the surprising behaviour stops being surprising.

title: Kubernetes by Example 04: Deployments and Rollouts
description: You asked for a rolling update and got a gap anyway. Here is what actually moves during a deploy, and what sets its pace.

title: Kubernetes by Example 05: DaemonSets
description: Three replicas gave you two pods on one machine and none on another. When the whole point is to be there , you need a different question.

title: Kubernetes by Example 06: StatefulSets and Jobs
description: Three database replicas with random names, fighting over one disk. Some pods need to be somebody — and some workloads aren't servers at all.

title: Kubernetes by Example 07: Services and Ingress
description: Every component is healthy, and nothing can reach anything. The object that knows why is one most people never look at.

title: Kubernetes by Example 08: Config and Secrets
description: You edited the ConfigMap. You confirmed it changed. The pod carried on with the old value, and will do so forever.

title: Kubernetes by Example 09: Storage
description: Three restarts overnight and the buffer was empty every time. The container filesystem is writable, and that is exactly the problem.

title: Kubernetes by Example 10: Requests, Limits and QoS
description: A pod killed with no error, and a node that is full at ten percent. Both are the same misunderstanding.

title: Kubernetes by Example 12: Staying Up

description: An autoscaler that will never scale, and a pod quietly forbidden from doing its job. Both report perfect health.
